target_customer: Developers and product teams that need to extract structured data from video without training models
problem: Building a custom video detection model normally needs labeled data and ML work. Dragoneye lets a developer describe what to detect and get a model without annotating or training.
business_model: Usage-based API and SDK with a subscription tier (a directory lists a starting price of $49 per month, unverified)
product_category: Zero-shot computer vision API for video

founders.name: Alex Liao
education: University of Pennsylvania, Physics and CS
founders.background_notes: Bio from the YC page. The page lists a team of 2 but names only one founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Delivering usable detection models from a text description with no training required open vocabulary vision models and video handling, hard for a two person team in 2024.

defensibility.rationale: Open vocabulary detection models and hosted vision APIs from larger vendors were available, so a thin wrapper was copyable. No customer lock in or data advantage is evidenced.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large vendors offered image and video detection services and zero-shot options. No sign they bought or copied Dragoneye specifically; it remains small.

market_need_then: Developers wanted vision features without labeling pipelines. Evidence of demand is thin: the site names no customers and the YC page gives no traction numbers.

identity.logo: A dragon eye mark (per the company site)
identity.visual_style: Developer tool site with a Playground demo
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and plain: Turn videos into data

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or merch about the brand was found. The name is distinctive but the brand has little visible reach.

outcome_analysis: Dragoneye is still active with a two person team as of the YC page. The product moved from custom video detection models toward zero-shot video to data extraction with an SDK and an MCP server for coding agents. No outside round could be verified, so its trajectory cannot be judged beyond staying small and shipping.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators (CB Insights, VCBacked, Extruct) say about $500K, mostly YC, dated around 2024-01 to 2024-03, one calling it a convertible note and another pre-seed. No primary source, so not recorded as a round. Competition: the search returned only 2025 and 2026 pages and generic vendor docs, nothing dated near the 2024-01 launch, so the list is empty. No outcome news found. Name origin not found. Update: the 2024-01 convertible note rests on CB Insights; VCBacked calls it pre-seed (announced 2024-03) and Extruct seed.
